transcript.text: Isn't that like using a metal detector to find out if there are unicorns in your sock drawer?

transcript.speaker: Skeptic
transcript.text: No!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Later that night

transcript.speaker: Skeptic
transcript.text: A skeptic checks all the drawers.

setting: A room with a table, later a bedroom with a dresser
situation: Dogbert questions a bearded, mustached skeptic about whether his controlled tests could ever detect psychic powers. Dogbert compares it to using a metal detector to look for unicorns in a sock drawer, and the skeptic angrily denies the comparison. That night, the skeptic is alone sweeping a metal detector over his dresser drawers.
punchline: The skeptic insists the analogy is wrong, but privately he is searching his drawers with a metal detector, showing that Dogbert's point hit home and that he is checking every possibility.
summary: A prickly debunker rejects a pointed analogy about his testing methods, then secretly sweeps his furniture with a metal detector to be thorough.

file: 1998/1998-10-02_tina tech writer_engineers_information requested_sow seeds_destruction_snarling_compose email.gif
title: Snarling While Writing Angry Email

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: To: All engineers. From: Tina the Tech Writer

transcript.speaker: Tina
transcript.text: Give me the information I requested, or sow the seeds of your own destruction!

transcript.speaker: Tina
transcript.text: One should never compose e-mail while one is snarling.

situation: Tina the tech writer types an email to all engineers demanding the information she requested, threatening them with dramatic language while snarling at her screen. In the last panel she calmly reflects, in a thought bubble, that it is unwise to write email while angry.
punchline: Tina realizes only after sending a melodramatic threat to the whole engineering team that she should not have written it while snarling.
summary: A tech writer fires off a theatrically menacing email to the engineers and then ponders the wisdom of emailing in a rage.

file: 1998/1998-11-25_teach morons_high level jobs_addicted to wagging_ear clokwise_tongue in.gif
title: Dogbert Trains Executives to Wag

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I'm going to teach morons how to get high-level jobs.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Why?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I'm addicted to wagging.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Carry on.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Now turn your ear clockwise to get your tongue back in.

setting: Dilbert's office, then a conference room
situation: Dogbert announces he will teach morons how to land high-level jobs. Dilbert asks why, and Dogbert admits he is addicted to wagging, so Dilbert hands him money and tells him to carry on. In the last panel Dogbert stands on a conference table instructing three executives who sit with their tongues sticking out and their hands on their ears.
punchline: Dogbert's get-rich scheme is to train gullible people into mindless executives, and the executives follow his absurd instructions so obediently that they are comically easy to fool.
summary: A scheming dog collects payment to coach clueless people into senior positions, and his pupils obey even the silliest commands.

file: 1998/1998-07-31_worthless employee_newspapaer artcicles_routes them around_articles relevant_more work_third stall.gif
title: Clipping Articles From Bathroom Newspaper

transcript.speaker: Clipper
transcript.text: I'm a worthless employee who cuts out newspaper articles and routes them around.

transcript.speaker: Clipper
transcript.text: I used to make sure the articles were relevant, but that was more work than it was worth.

transcript.speaker: Bald Coworker
transcript.text: I saw this already.

transcript.speaker: Clipper
transcript.text: It's from your paper. You always leave it in the third stall.

situation: A tie-wearing employee with scissors introduces himself to a bald, bespectacled coworker as a worthless employee who clips newspaper articles and routes them around. He admits he stopped checking whether the articles were relevant because it was too much effort. When the coworker says he has already seen the clipping, the clipper reveals it came from the coworker's own newspaper, which he leaves in the bathroom's third stall.
punchline: The clipper's lazy routing scheme is so careless that he even circulates articles taken from his coworker's own newspaper, which the coworker leaves in a bathroom stall.
summary: A self-described useless clipper hands out newspaper cuttings without any screening, even recycling ones swiped from a colleague's restroom reading material.

file: 1998/1998-04-08_request denied_information servvces_non standard computers_replacement_discard the old one_trash declined_no computers.gif
title: Discarding Old Computer Is Impossible

transcript.speaker: IS Manager
transcript.text: Request denied. The Information Services Department does not upgrade non-standard computers.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: It's not an upgrade. It's a replacement.

transcript.speaker: IS Manager
transcript.text: Our policy is that it's an upgrade unless you discard the old one.

transcript.speaker: Garbage Man
transcript.text: Your trash is declined. Our policy is "No computers."

setting: IS manager's office and a loading area with a garbage bin
situation: Dilbert asks the Information Services manager to upgrade his non-standard computer and is refused. He argues it's a replacement, and the manager says it only counts as a replacement if he discards the old machine. When Dilbert tries to throw the old computer away, the garbage man refuses it because of a no-computers policy.
punchline: Two conflicting bureaucratic policies leave Dilbert trapped in a catch-22: he can't get a new computer without discarding the old one, and he can't discard the old one anywhere.
summary: A bureaucratic loop leaves an employee unable to get a new computer because nobody will take the old one.

file: 1998/1998-08-02_performance review_met objectives_packed schedule_urgent_handle this_sample of handwriting.gif
title: Boss's Urgent Notes Fill Dilbert's Schedule

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Let's see how many of your objectives you met.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: What objectives?

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Didn't you know you had objectives?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I don't see how I would have had time to work on objectives.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: My schedule was packed.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Doing what?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Every morning you leave things on my chair with notes that say "Urgent: Handle this."

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: No I don't.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Wally, can I see a sample of your handwriting?

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Uh-oh.

setting: The Boss's office during a performance review, then Wally's cubicle
situation: During his performance review, Dilbert learns he was supposed to have objectives and says he had no time because his schedule was full of urgent tasks left on his chair each morning. The Boss denies leaving any such notes. Dilbert then goes to Wally and asks for a sample of his handwriting, suspecting him of leaving the notes.
punchline: Dilbert realizes that Wally has been secretly dumping his own work on him with fake urgent notes, and Wally's "Uh-oh" confirms he's guilty.
summary: Buried in anonymous urgent tasks and judged on goals he never knew about, Dilbert hunts down the real culprit behind the notes.

file: 1998/1998-03-28_underfunded porject_resources_intern_sponge bath_water fountain_employees_budget diffrences_business.gif
title: Underfunded Project Employee Begs Resources

transcript.speaker: Ragged Employee
transcript.text: I hate being on an underfunded project.

transcript.speaker: Ragged Employee
transcript.text: Can you spare some resources, lady? How about that intern? Are you using him?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: First you have to learn how to give yourself a sponge bath at the water fountain.

setting: Office corridor near a water fountain
situation: A scruffy, tattered employee with a blue headband sits on the floor thinking about how bad his underfunded project is. He then panhandles a well-funded manager, asking her to spare resources like her intern. Dilbert replies, and the ragged man demonstrates washing himself at the water fountain.
punchline: The underfunded project team is so destitute that they live like homeless people, and getting extra resources apparently requires first mastering survival skills like bathing in the water fountain.
summary: A project starved of budget reduces its staff to ragged beggars who must scrounge for help and wash at the office water fountain.

file: 1998/1998-10-05_misses staff meeting_buy donuts_freedom donuts.gif
title: Donuts Penalty For Missing Meetings

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: From now on, anyone who misses a staff meeting must buy donuts for the next meeting.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Did I just sell them their freedom for donuts?

setting: Conference room during a staff meeting
situation: The Boss announces a new rule at a staff meeting: anyone who misses a meeting must bring donuts to the next one. Dilbert, Wally and Alice sit quietly listening. Once the room empties, the Boss privately wonders whether his rule has just given employees a cheap way to skip meetings.
punchline: The Boss realizes that his intended punishment actually lets employees buy their way out of meetings for the price of donuts, making absence a bargain.
summary: A manager tries to enforce meeting attendance with a donut fine, then suspects he has accidentally made skipping meetings affordable.

file: 1998/1998-03-07_excellent job_projects assigned_fifty hours a day_adequate_complete fiduciary misconduct.gif
title: Alice Calculates Impossible Workload Hours

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: I estimated the hours it would take to do an excellent job on all the projects you've assigned.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: That would be fifty hours a day. So I recalculated for "adequate" results. That would be forty hours per day.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Well, to make a long story short, let's skip down to "complete fiduciary misconduct."

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Blah blah blah blah blah

situation: Alice presents the Boss with her calculations of how many hours per day it would take to finish all the projects he has assigned her. Even settling for merely adequate work would require forty hours a day, so she skips ahead to the level of work that is actually feasible. The Boss tunes her out, holding his head and muttering blah blah.
punchline: Since the workload is impossible, Alice says the only achievable result is negligent, fraudulent-level work, and the Boss is too checked out to listen to the warning.
summary: An overloaded employee shows her manager that his assignments demand more hours than exist in a day, and the only realistic outcome she can offer is gross negligence.

file: 1998/1998-08-31_weasel_store clerk_never settle_lesser of two weasels.gif
title: Never Settle for Lesser Weasel

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: It's nice, but the weasel down the street is selling it for less.

transcript.speaker: Weasel Salesman
transcript.text: You should never settle for the lesser of two weasels.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Now that you mention it, it DID seem too convenient.

setting: An electronics store, then Dilbert's living room
situation: Dilbert is in an electronics store holding a gadget and tells the weasel salesman that a competing weasel down the street sells it cheaper. The salesman answers with a pun that he should never settle for the lesser of two weasels. Dilbert, now at home on the couch with Dogbert beside him, reconsiders and decides the whole offer seemed too convenient.
punchline: The salesman's wordplay on 'lesser of two evils' is so transparently manipulative that Dilbert is persuaded the deal was suspicious, which is the opposite of what the salesman intended.
summary: A shopper haggling with a sneaky salesman gets a clumsy pun for a sales pitch and concludes the whole deal smells fishy.

file: 1998/1998-05-27_no charismatic leaders_cable tv_scandal_diversion_great news story_fertility drugs_in coffee.gif
title: Dogbert Spikes Dilbert's Coffee With Fertility Drugs

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Why are there no charismatic leaders anymore?

transcript.speaker: Garbage Man
transcript.text: Cable TV.

transcript.speaker: Garbage Man
transcript.text: Scandal is the most economical way to fill news programs. They'll go after you, too.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I'll need a diversion.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I don't care if it's a great news story; I will NOT take fertility drugs!

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: They're in your coffee.

setting: Outside beside a garbage can, then Dilbert's home
situation: Dogbert, wearing a crown and sitting on a garbage can, asks a garbage man why there are no charismatic leaders anymore. The garbage man blames cable TV and warns that scandal-hungry news programs will come after Dogbert too. Dogbert decides he needs a diversion, and in the last panel Dilbert loudly refuses to take fertility drugs as a news story, while Dogbert reveals the drugs are already in his coffee.
punchline: Dogbert creates his diversion from media scrutiny by secretly dosing Dilbert's coffee with fertility drugs, making Dilbert the scandalous news story instead.
summary: A crowned Dogbert, warned that the media hunts for scandal, deflects attention by quietly turning his friend into the headline.

file: 1998/1998-03-12_albanian factory tour_sweat shop_companys prodcut_attach clamps_cubicles_damaged morale.gif
title: Elbonian Sweatshop Clamps Replace Cubicles

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Elbonian factory tour

transcript.speaker: Elbonian Guide
transcript.text: This is the sweat shop where we make your company's product.

transcript.speaker: Elbonian Guide
transcript.text: We attach huge clamps to each employee's head.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Why?

transcript.speaker: Elbonian Guide
transcript.text: We tried cubicles but it damaged morale.

setting: Elbonian factory (sweat shop), outdoors in a muddy landscape
situation: Alice takes notes while an Elbonian guide shows her around the sweat shop that produces her company's product. She sees workers with huge clamps attached to their heads and asks why. The guide explains that they used to use cubicles, but those hurt morale.
punchline: The Elbonians consider cubicles too demoralizing for workers, yet see nothing wrong with clamping heads, a jab at how bad cubicles are by comparison.
summary: A visiting employee learns that an overseas factory clamps its workers' heads because the alternative, office cubicles, was judged too depressing.

file: 1998/1998-02-23_hidden qaulities_act humble_deitful_manipulative_hypocritical braggart_funny world.gif
title: Humbly Bragging Your Hidden Qualities

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I believe it's what's inside a person that counts.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: How can you get respect for hidden qualities?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: You have to act humble while generating as many clues as possible.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: So, you recommend being a deceitful, manipulative, hypocritical braggart?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: It's a funny world.

setting: Outdoor path and rocks in a park
situation: Dilbert walks outside with Dogbert and says that inner qualities are what matter. Dogbert asks how anyone can earn respect for qualities nobody can see, and Dilbert explains that you must appear humble while dropping as many hints as possible about your virtues. Dogbert sums this up as being a deceitful, manipulative, hypocritical braggart.
punchline: Dilbert's advice for getting credit for your hidden virtues amounts to fake modesty and covert bragging, which Dilbert shrugs off as just how the world works.
summary: A walk in the park turns into a cynical lesson on how pretending to be modest is the best way to advertise your good traits.

file: 1998/1998-05-08_united nations_billion dollars_donated_france_dogbert.gif
title: Dogbert Renames France at UN

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I donated a billion dollars to the United Nations today.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: That's nice of you.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: My only condition is that they name something after me.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: United Nations

transcript.speaker: UN Delegate
transcript.text: For the millionth time: Yes, I'm SURE we want to keep calling it France!

setting: Dilbert's living room couch, then a United Nations meeting room
situation: Dogbert tells Dilbert, who is snacking on the couch, that he has donated a billion dollars to the United Nations. His only condition is that they name something after him. At the UN, the French delegate, seated at the France placard, is exasperated at having to repeatedly confirm that they want to keep the name France.
punchline: Dogbert's donation condition implies he demanded that France be renamed after him, leaving the French delegate fed up with refusing the offer over and over.
summary: A wealthy Dogbert buys naming rights from the UN, and the beleaguered French representative is stuck rejecting a rebrand of his entire country.

file: 1998/1998-01-21_sales force_retirement buyout_fifty dollars_meeting_boss_business.gif
title: Salespeople Accept Fifty Dollar Buyout

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: The sales force was offered a retirement buyout package of fifty dollars.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: One hundred percent of the sales force elected to take the offer.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I wonder what they know that I don't know.

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: There's a hole with no bottom.

setting: Conference room during a management meeting
situation: The Boss reads from a report to two colleagues at a conference table. He announces that the entire sales force was offered a tiny fifty-dollar retirement buyout and every one of them accepted. He wonders aloud what the departing salespeople know that he doesn't, and a coworker remarks that he is a bottomless pit of ignorance.
punchline: The Boss cannot work out why everyone took an absurdly small buyout, and a colleague sarcastically points out that his cluelessness is bottomless.
summary: A manager is baffled that every salesperson grabbed a laughably small payout to leave, and a colleague gently mocks his obliviousness.

file: 1998/1998-01-04_drunk_out of control_on a date_can't get date_whose idea.gif
title: Never Drunk, Never In Control

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'll never get drunk. I don't want to be out of control.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Are you in control at work?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Well... no.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Are you in control when you're on a date?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I can't get a date.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: And whose idea was it to go on this walk?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Yours.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Are you saying I should get drunk?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: No, no.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I'm saying the decision will be made by the beer companies.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I hope they say it's okay.

setting: A grassy path on an autumn walk outdoors
situation: Dilbert and Dogbert take a walk while Dilbert claims he'll never get drunk because he hates being out of control. Dogbert points out that Dilbert is not in control at work, on dates, or even of where he walks. Dogbert concludes that the beer companies, not Dilbert, will make the decision.
punchline: Dilbert's life is already so controlled by others that his claim of staying in control is meaningless, and he even hopes the beer companies will approve of his drinking.
summary: A man's boast about always staying in control crumbles as his dog lists every area of life where someone else calls the shots.

file: 1998/1998-12-29_sadistic nut_dennis_insulting_sadistic_meeting_assume skills_thousand dead camels_rotting flesh_business.gif
title: Why Tolerate the Sadistic Nut

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: The Sadistic Nut

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Are there any questions?

transcript.speaker: Sadistic Nut
transcript.text: Why does your body lotion smell like the rotting flesh of a thousand dead camels?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I assume he has valuable skills.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: No, you're thinking of a prima donna.

situation: At a meeting, a woman asks if there are any questions. An angry, scowling coworker known as the Sadistic Nut responds with a bizarre insult about her body lotion smelling like rotting camel flesh. Dilbert wonders why the company tolerates him, and Wally corrects the assumption.
punchline: Companies tolerate abusive prima donnas because they have valuable skills, but the Sadistic Nut has none, so there is no excuse for keeping him.
summary: A hostile coworker hurls an absurd insult at a colleague, and a coworker's guess that he must be talented is shot down as confusing him with a different kind of difficult employee.

file: 1998/1998-12-21_supermodel_trouble finding dates_men are intimidated_beauty_computer skills_system adminstartor_health.gif
title: Chatting With a Supermodel Online

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm chatting with a supermodel who has trouble finding dates.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: She says men are intimidated by her beauty and her computer skills.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Dang! The system administrator is making a move on her.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Type faster!

setting: Dilbert's office cubicle, at his computer
situation: Dilbert sits at his computer chatting online with a supermodel who says men are intimidated by her looks and computer skills. Midway through the chat, he realizes the system administrator is also chatting with her and hitting on her. Dogbert urges him to type faster to beat the rival.
punchline: The supermodel's claim that men are intimidated is undercut by the fact that the chat is full of lonely, computer-savvy men competing for her attention, with Dilbert racing the system administrator.
summary: While messaging a glamorous stranger online, a nerdy engineer discovers the network's admin is moving in on her, and his dog tells him to hurry.

file: 1998/1998-10-16_catbert the hr director_groom for management_bugs in fur_lick head_can't be manager.gif
title: Grooming Asok for Management Literally

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Catbert the H.R. Director

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Asok, it's time to groom you for management.

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: I don't see too many bugs in your fur.

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Can you lick the top of your own head?

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: No, I can't.

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Then you can't be a manager.

situation: Catbert, the H.R. Director, tells Asok it is time to groom him for management, then takes the phrase literally and inspects Asok's hair for bugs. He asks whether Asok can lick the top of his own head, and when Asok admits he cannot, Catbert disqualifies him from becoming a manager.
punchline: Catbert twists the corporate phrase 'groom for management' into literal cat grooming and invents an absurd, arbitrary qualification, mocking how random and meaningless promotion criteria can be.
summary: An H.R. cat takes the idea of preparing an employee for promotion literally and rejects him over a feline grooming test.

file: 1998/1998-06-02_severe shyness_nude photos_internet_previous clients_motley crue_dogbert_technology.gif
title: Dogbert's Questionable Shyness Therapy

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I've been having severe shyness attacks at work.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I can help.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I'll send nude photos of you to everyone on the Internet.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Will that work?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: All of my previous clients are dating "Mötley Crüe" band members.

setting: Dilbert's bedroom, with both characters in bed
situation: Dilbert tells Dogbert, who is acting as a consultant or therapist, that he suffers from severe shyness at work. Dogbert proposes to cure it by sending nude photos of Dilbert to everyone on the Internet. When Dilbert asks if it will work, Dogbert cites his previous clients' success.
punchline: Dogbert's outrageous cure is justified by the claim that his past clients now date rock musicians, implying that humiliating exposure brings celebrity attention and dating success.
summary: A shy Dilbert gets an absurdly invasive cure from Dogbert, who backs it up with a glamorous track record of rock-star romances.

file: 1998/1998-05-07_promise customers_product not yet designed_motto_ask forgiveness_seek permission_design work.gif
title: Marketing Motto Needs Design Work

transcript.speaker: Man in blue tie
transcript.text: Maybe it was wrong to promise our customers a product that hasn't been designed yet.

transcript.speaker: Marketing woman
transcript.text: But our motto in Marketing is, "It's better to ask for forgiveness than to seek permission."

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Your motto needs some design work too.

situation: A coworker suggests it was a mistake to promise customers a product that hasn't been designed yet. The big-haired Marketing woman defends herself with her department's motto about asking forgiveness rather than permission. Dilbert, standing on the roof with them, responds that the motto itself needs design work.
punchline: Dilbert turns the designer's complaint back on Marketing, sarcastically implying their motto is as poorly thought out as the product they sold before it existed.
summary: Marketing justifies selling a nonexistent product with a reckless slogan, and Dilbert dryly mocks the slogan as being just as unfinished.

file: 1998/1998-07-04_socially defective_unique preferences_arguments_dating_girl_dilbert defending himself_relationships.gif
title: Dilbert Calls Date Socially Defective

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I don't understand why you like the things you like.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm forced to conclude that you're socially defective.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Isn't it normal for people to have unique preferences?

transcript.speaker: Girl
transcript.text: Do you have to argue with everything I say?!

setting: Outdoors, walking beside a low stone wall
situation: Dilbert is out with a blonde woman and tells her he cannot understand why she likes the things she likes. He then concludes she is socially defective for having different tastes. When he asks if unique preferences are normal, she objects that he argues with everything she says.
punchline: Dilbert's own question about unique preferences is the argument she was making, and he fails to see that he is the one being contrary and socially clumsy.
summary: A man on a date dismisses his companion's tastes as a defect, then accidentally defends individuality while she calls out his constant arguing.

file: 1998/1998-01-03_nobel prize_garbage industry_miss the smells_paper plate.gif
title: Garbage Man Won't Leave Garbage

transcript.speaker: Ratbert
transcript.text: Now that you've won the Nobel Prize, I guess you'll leave the garbage industry.

transcript.speaker: Garbage Man
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Garbage Man
transcript.text: I'd miss the action. I'd miss the smells... the sights... the people...

transcript.speaker: Ratbert
transcript.text: ...the rats.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I accidentally threw out a paper plate last week. Would you look for it?

transcript.speaker: Garbage Man
transcript.text: I'm kidding about the people part.

setting: Outdoors by garbage cans on a residential street
situation: Ratbert asks the garbage man, who has just won a Nobel Prize, whether he will quit the garbage industry. He says no and lists the things he would miss, including the smells and the sights. A homeowner then asks him to search for a paper plate she accidentally threw out.
punchline: The garbage man loves the job but admits he was kidding about missing the people, since the people's absurd requests, like digging for a lost paper plate, are the worst part.
summary: A Nobel-winning garbage collector explains why he'd never quit his trade, until a customer's silly request reveals what he really dislikes about it.

file: 1998/1998-12-07_asok_alice_report to alice_email_difficult communications.gif
title: Boss Delegates Asok to Alice

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: From now on, Asok, you'll report to Alice instead of me.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: You can never directly speak to me again. Everything must go through Alice.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Tell him I understand.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Submit your request by e-mail.

situation: The Boss announces that Asok will now report to Alice and forbids Asok from ever speaking to him directly. When Asok stands there, the Boss tells Alice to relay that he understands, and Alice, working at her computer, coldly tells Asok to submit his request by e-mail.
punchline: The Boss avoids even talking to Asok while standing right beside him, passing messages through Alice, who then adds her own bureaucratic layer by demanding an e-mail request.
summary: A manager hands off an employee to a coworker and then refuses to communicate with him except through that intermediary, even while standing next to him.

file: 1998/1998-04-11_accept transfer_frozen asteroid_surplussed_map.gif
title: Tiny Island Where Caring People Live

transcript.speaker: Ted
transcript.text: If I don't accept the transfer to a frozen asteroid, I'll be surplussed.

transcript.speaker: Tina
transcript.text: Ted, let me show you something on this map.

transcript.speaker: Tina
transcript.text: See this tiny island?

transcript.speaker: Ted
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Tina
transcript.text: That's where the people who care live.

situation: Ted tells Tina he must accept a transfer to a frozen asteroid or be laid off as surplus. Instead of sympathizing, Tina unfolds a map and points to a tiny island, telling him that is where the people who care live.
punchline: Tina sarcastically shows that the number of people who care about Ted's predicament is vanishingly small, and she is not one of them.
summary: A worker faces an absurd forced relocation or layoff, and a coworker responds by mapping out how few people sympathize.

file: 1998/1998-01-08_free thursday_surprise party_flowers_card_snowballed_good taste_karaoke.gif
title: Karaoke at a Grieving Coworker's Party

transcript.speaker: Carol
transcript.text: Are you free on Thursday for Ted's surprise party?

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Party? You don't give a party for someone who has a death in the family.

transcript.speaker: Carol
transcript.text: Well... we got him a card, then flowers. It just snowballed.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I assume this will all be in good taste.

transcript.speaker: Carol
transcript.text: I can't promise that. Karaoke is really hit or miss.

situation: Carol asks a coworker if he is free for Ted's surprise party, and he points out that you don't throw a party for someone who has just suffered a death in the family. She explains that the card and flowers escalated into a party. When he hopes it will be tasteful, she admits there will be karaoke.
punchline: An office sympathy gesture has escalated into a party for a bereaved coworker, and the planned karaoke makes good taste impossible to guarantee.
summary: A well-meaning office gift collection for a grieving colleague has grown out of control into a surprise karaoke party.

file: 1998/1998-07-05_posterior_fat ass_chair_prnak_lied boss_like goldfish_big charis_big ass.gif
title: Posteriors Grow Like Goldfish

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: My posterior is growing to fit the size of my chair.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Is that possible?

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Posteriors are like goldfish. They grow to the limit of their environment.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: That's ridiculous. I have the biggest chair. That would mean...

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Forget I brought it up.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Well, back to work.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Mission report.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Success.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: The glue on his chair should be set by now.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I guess this is why goldfishes don't use chairs.

setting: The Boss's office and Alice's cubicle area
situation: Alice tells the Boss that posteriors grow to fit the size of their chair, like goldfish. The Boss, who has the biggest chair, realizes the implication and abruptly drops the subject. Alice then reports mission success to Dilbert and Dogbert, having glued the chair to his rear; the Boss ends up carrying the chair on his back.
punchline: Alice's prank leaves the Boss glued to his oversized chair, and he muses that this is why goldfish don't use chairs.
summary: After a barb about oversized chairs and widening backsides, Alice secretly glues the Boss to his big chair and he ends up lugging it around.

file: 1998/1998-12-28_boss hires dennis_indispensable_sadistic nut_job unbearable_die in own vomit!.gif
title: Boss Hires Sadistic Nut Deliberately

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Every work group has one sadistic nut who makes the job unbearable for everyone else.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: That's why I hired Dennis.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: He already seems indispensable.

transcript.speaker: Dennis
transcript.text: You'll all die in your own vomit!

situation: The Boss lectures Alice and Dilbert that every team has one sadistic person who makes work miserable. He then reveals he deliberately hired a new employee, Dennis, to fill that role. Dennis, scowling and sticking out his tongue, screams a vile threat at the team while the Boss approves.
punchline: The Boss treats a hostile, abusive employee as a valuable asset and hires one on purpose, deciding he is already indispensable because he makes everyone's job unbearable.
summary: A manager proudly recruits a nasty new hire to fill the team's supposedly mandatory role of workplace tormentor.

file: 1998/1998-01-16_skeptics association_rats claims_bad experinces_jurors_oj simpson trial_debunk_hubble telescope.gif
title: Skeptic Debunks Rat's ESP Claims

transcript.speaker: Man with mustache
transcript.text: I'm glad the "Skeptics Association" sent you to debunk my rat's claims of ESP.

transcript.speaker: Man with mustache
transcript.text: The others don't go out much since their bad experiences as jurors on the O.J. Simpson trial.

transcript.speaker: Man with mustache
transcript.text: Well, I'm glad you could make it.

transcript.speaker: Skeptic
transcript.text: Let's hurry. I have to debunk the so-called Hubble telescope later today.

setting: Home of a man with a mustache, near a coat rack
situation: A man with a mustache welcomes Dilbert, who has been sent by the Skeptics Association to debunk his pet rat's claims of ESP. The man explains that the other skeptics rarely go out since serving as jurors on the O.J. Simpson trial. Dilbert hangs up his coat and says he must hurry because he is also scheduled to debunk the Hubble telescope.
punchline: The skeptics are so reflexively dismissive that their schedule includes debunking even the Hubble telescope, an obviously real and verified instrument, and the O.J. jury reference implies they are the kind of people who reject evidence.
summary: A professional doubter arrives to dismiss a rat's psychic powers, then reveals he plans to dismiss a famous space telescope too.

file: 1998/1998-07-07_share hotel rooms_conference_roomie_agree to rules_spoon on right_sleep together_buddies_new rules_cheap company.gif
title: Wally's Roommate Rules: Spooning Only Right

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Wally, as you know, employees must share hotel rooms at the conference...

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: So I was wondering if you'd like to... you know... be my roomie.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Sure.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: We'll have to agree on some rules.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I can only spoon on my right.

situation: Dilbert awkwardly asks Wally to be his roommate at an upcoming conference, since the company requires employees to share hotel rooms. Wally agrees casually, and when Dilbert says they need ground rules, Wally offers his own bizarre condition about spooning.
punchline: Wally treats the rules for sharing a hotel room as being about spooning, implying he assumes they will cuddle in bed, which is exactly what Dilbert did not mean.
summary: A cost-cutting travel policy forces two coworkers to bunk together, and one of them has an alarmingly intimate idea of roommate etiquette.

file: 1998/1998-07-15_son-of_a_boss_simple prodcut_mom can use_hamster_simple_dumb_leave mom out_physicist.gif
title: Son-of-a-Boss Insults Engineer's Mother

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Son-of-a-Boss

transcript.speaker: Son-of-a-Boss
transcript.text: You have to make our product so simple that my mom could use it.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: It's already so simple a hamster could use it. How much dumber is your mom?

transcript.speaker: Son-of-a-Boss
transcript.text: Maybe we should leave my mom out of this.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: My mom is a physicist.

situation: The Boss's son, a young manager, tells Alice to make the company's product simple enough for his mom to use. Alice replies that it is already hamster-simple and asks how much dumber his mom is. When he objects to the insult, she counters by pointing out that her own mom is a physicist.
punchline: Alice turns the boss's son's demand into an insult about his mother's intelligence, and then trumps his protest by noting her own mom is a physicist, implying his mom is far less capable.
summary: A manager's demand for foolproof simplicity gets a withering comeback about his mother's intelligence compared to Alice's scientist mom.
keywords: leave my mom out of this

file: 1998/1998-06-30_dogebrts tech support_email_tech support guy_classical music_mister radio.gif
title: Tech Support Suggests Raising Your IQ

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Dogbert's Tech Support

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I don't know how to use my e-mail.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: You need to upgrade your I.Q. a few points. Try listening to classical music.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: My old nemesis, Mister Radio, we meet again.

setting: Office cubicle and Dogbert's tech support desk
situation: A man phones Dogbert's tech support because he cannot work his e-mail. Dogbert tells him the problem is his intelligence and advises him to listen to classical music to boost his IQ. The caller then glares at a small radio on a shelf, treating it as an old enemy he must confront.
punchline: Dogbert insults the caller's intelligence instead of helping, and the caller's dramatic grudge against a mere radio shows he really is not very bright.
summary: Instead of solving an e-mail problem, a tech support dog prescribes highbrow music, sending the befuddled caller into a showdown with his radio.

file: 1998/1998-06-22_no one wants job_village_fillage_dogbert as ceo.gif
title: Dogbert CEO Plans to Pillage

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Mister Dogbert has returned as our C.E.O. because no one else wants the job.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I can't tell you my plan for the assets of this company... but it rhymes with "village."

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I hope it's "fillage."

situation: The Boss announces at a board meeting that Dogbert has returned as CEO only because nobody else would take the job. Dogbert hints that his plan for the company's assets rhymes with "village." Afterward, an employee, standing beside Dilbert, hopefully guesses "fillage."
punchline: Dogbert is obviously planning to pillage the company's assets, but the naive employee hopes for the harmless-sounding "fillage" instead.
summary: A returning dog executive teases a plan for company assets that rhymes with a word for looting, and a hopeful underling guesses a nonsense alternative.

file: 1998/1998-06-29_budget froecast_missing_dilbert_the boss_sat on dcoument.gif
title: Budget Forecast Stuck To Boss

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Where's that budget forecast I asked for?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I put it on your chair this morning.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I'd better look again.

situation: The Boss pokes his head into Dilbert's cubicle and demands the budget forecast he requested. Dilbert says he left it on the Boss's chair that morning. The Boss walks away, thinking he should look again, while a sheet of paper is visibly stuck to the seat of his pants.
punchline: The Boss has been sitting on the missing budget forecast all along and it is stuck to his backside, yet he is too oblivious to realize it.
summary: A manager hunting for a document he already sat on heads off to search again, with the paper plainly stuck to his trousers.

file: 1998/1998-02-14_sex symbol_wats inside_doesn't count_philosopher_point.gif
title: Dogbert's Shallow Sex Symbol Philosophy

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: How does it feel to be a sex symbol?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Good.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I realized that what's inside a person doesn't count because no one can see it.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I didn't realize you were such a philosopher.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: That's my point!

setting: Dilbert's living room, with Dogbert on the couch
situation: Dilbert is reading a Playgirl magazine that features Dogbert on the cover, and asks Dogbert how it feels to be a sex symbol. Dogbert explains that he has concluded a person's insides don't matter since nobody can see them. Dilbert remarks that Dogbert is quite a philosopher, and Dogbert replies that this is exactly his point.
punchline: Dogbert's apparent philosophical depth is actually a rationalization for valuing only appearance, and he points out that Dilbert's praise of his deep thinking proves that inner qualities go unnoticed.
summary: A dog turned magazine pin-up justifies his fame by arguing that hidden inner qualities are worthless, then uses Dilbert's compliment about his wisdom as proof.

file: 1998/1998-05-30_fertility drug_doctors office_babies_woman involved_diapers_prescription_painful shots.gif
title: Dilbert Asks Doctor About Giving Birth

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: My dog slipped me a fertility drug. How soon before I give birth?

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Um... it's impossible to have babies unless a woman is involved in some way.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Ooh, right, for the diapers.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: I'm going to give you a prescription for painful shots.

situation: Dilbert sits on the exam table and tells his doctor that Dogbert slipped him a fertility drug, asking how soon he will give birth. The doctor explains that a woman must be involved in having babies, and Dilbert misunderstands, thinking she means someone is needed for diapers. The exasperated doctor responds by prescribing painful shots.
punchline: Dilbert's obtuse misunderstanding of basic biology is so exasperating that the doctor retaliates by prescribing painful shots as a cheerful punishment.
summary: A man who believes he's pregnant from a pet-administered drug gets a biology lesson he misreads, and his doctor settles the matter with a vengeful prescription.

file: 1998/1998-06-01_telephone shyness_make business calls_restroom_shyness passes_dilbert_office.gif
title: Dilbert Hides From Phone Calls

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm having a severe case of telephone shyness.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm afraid to pick up the phone and make business calls.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'll duck into a restroom stall until the shyness passes.

setting: Dilbert's office cubicle, then the restroom door in the hallway
situation: Dilbert sits at his desk thinking to himself that he has a severe case of telephone shyness and is afraid to make business calls. Rather than facing the task, he decides to hide in a restroom stall until the feeling goes away, and he heads for the restroom door.
punchline: Dilbert treats his avoidance of an unpleasant work task as a medical-sounding condition and plans to wait it out in a bathroom stall, which is just procrastination dressed up as a diagnosis.
summary: Faced with a dreaded round of business calls, Dilbert diagnoses himself with a fear of phones and slips away to hide in the restroom.

file: 1998/1998-03-04_sales conference_presentation_no user interface_computer_no bulky user manual_power outage_good from evil_technology.gif
title: Product With No User Interface

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Sales conference

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Here's the product you'll be selling next quarter.

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: It has NO user interface!

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: That means no bulky user manual. And no loss of function during a power outage!

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: You were right. Our sales people can't distinguish good from evil.

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: I strained a smile muscle.

transcript.speaker: Audience
transcript.text: Clap clap clap clap

setting: A sales conference room where a new product is being presented
situation: At a sales conference, Dilbert and a bald engineer present a computer product that has no user interface, spinning the missing features as benefits like no manual and no loss of function in a power outage. The sales audience applauds enthusiastically. Dilbert remarks that the engineer was right about the salespeople.
punchline: The salespeople applaud an obviously useless product with a spun-up pitch, showing they are too gullible to tell a good product from an evil one, and the engineer is amused enough to strain a smile muscle.
summary: Engineers pitch a blank, useless gadget as a feature-packed bargain, and the sales force cheers it on without question.

file: 1998/1998-12-23_dating a supermodel_camera adds pounds_adds makeup_adds hair.gif
title: Dating a Skeletal Supermodel

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Dating a supermodel

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I hear the camera adds...um... eighty pounds?

transcript.speaker: Supermodel
transcript.text: Yes. And if you use black and white film, the camera adds makeup too.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Does the camera add hair?

transcript.speaker: Supermodel
transcript.text: Why would it need to?

setting: A restaurant table during a date
situation: Dilbert is on a date with a supermodel who is drawn as a skeleton with a few strands of hair. He awkwardly asks about the saying that cameras add weight, and she answers in a deadpan way. He then asks whether the camera also adds hair.
punchline: The supermodel is so painfully thin that she is literally a skeleton, so she cheerfully agrees the camera must add pounds, and her reply shows she is oblivious to how bald and bony she looks.
summary: A nervous man on a date with a skeletal fashion model fumbles through small talk about how cameras flatter, only to be answered with unfazed vanity.

file: 1998/1998-08-27_worthless manager_project reveiwed_marking done.gif
title: Skipping the Worthless Manager Review

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: At this phase, the project will be reviewed by a worthless manager.

transcript.speaker: Manager
transcript.text: Hee-hee! I wonder if he knows what people say about him.

transcript.speaker: Manager
transcript.text: Why are you marking it "done"? Did you decide to skip that phase?

setting: Office desk with a project flowchart
situation: Dilbert walks a manager through a project flowchart and says the next phase involves review by a worthless manager. The manager laughs, wondering whether that person knows his reputation. When Dilbert marks the phase as done, the manager asks if he is skipping it.
punchline: The manager fails to realize that he is the worthless manager Dilbert means, so he is amused by the insult and then confused when the review phase is skipped.
summary: A manager chuckles at the idea of a useless reviewer, never realizing he is the one being described when Dilbert checks that step off.

file: 1998/1998-09-30_need by tomorrow_work all night_sound grateful_boss_last minute assignment_put upoin_asks dilbert_ungrateful boss.gif
title: Boss Demands Gratitude For Last-Minute Work

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: This is urgent. I need it by tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: You've known about this for weeks. Now I'll have to work all night!

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Could you at least say something that sounds grateful?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm glad I'm me!

situation: The Boss hands Dilbert a document and says he needs it finished by tomorrow. Dilbert complains that the Boss has known about the task for weeks and now he must work all night. The Boss asks him to at least sound grateful, and Dilbert answers that he is glad he is himself and not the Boss.
punchline: Dilbert's 'grateful' reply is a sarcastic insult implying that he is relieved not to be the Boss, who is clueless and poor at planning.
summary: A manager dumps an overdue task on an employee at the last minute, then asks for a thankful attitude and gets a cutting remark instead.

file: 1998/1998-04-23_cartoonist_ceo_conference_dilbert_key note speakers_politician_useful content.gif
title: Conference With No Useful Content

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: At the conference

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: They have some great keynote speakers here.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: There's a CEO... a politician... another CEO... and a cartoonist.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: In this cartoon, Gilbert goes to a conference that has no useful content.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I know guys like that.

setting: A business conference, from the registration desk to an escalator to an auditorium
situation: Dilbert arrives at a conference and reads the program, pleased with the lineup of keynote speakers. After he rides the escalator listing them, the cartoonist among them takes the stage and jokes that in this cartoon a character goes to a conference with no useful content. Dilbert, sitting in the audience, thinks he knows people like that.
punchline: The keynote cartoonist sarcastically admits the conference is worthless, and Dilbert, oblivious to the self-referential joke, thinks the speaker is talking about someone else.
summary: A hopeful conference-goer listens as the cartoonist headlining the event casually declares that the whole affair has nothing of value to offer.

file: 1998/1998-09-02_work nights_work weekends_quit_clear out desk_inspire_boss tells engineers.gif
title: Inspirational Speech Triggers Mass Resignation

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: We can only succeed if each of you works nights and weekends for a year!

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I quit.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Me too.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I'll clear out my desk.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Or was that supposed to inspire us?

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Like I'd know.

situation: The Boss tells his staff that the project can only succeed if everyone works nights and weekends for an entire year. Dilbert, Alice and Wally respond one after another that they quit and will clear out their desks. Dilbert then sarcastically asks whether the speech was meant to inspire them, and Alice says she wouldn't know.
punchline: The Boss's demand for a year of unpaid overtime is presented as a rallying cry, but the employees treat it as an obvious reason to quit, with Dilbert sarcastically wondering if it was meant to be motivational.
summary: A manager's demand for a year of nonstop overtime gets a chorus of resignations and a sarcastic question about whether it was meant as a pep talk.

file: 1998/1998-09-11_consulting job_wealthy_cuter_spreading disease_dilbert and rat.gif
title: Ratbert Claims Superiority Over Dilbert

transcript.speaker: Ratbert
transcript.text: Thanks to my consulting job, I'm wealthier than you.

transcript.speaker: Ratbert
transcript.text: And I'm cuter, obviously. The only thing left is personality.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Shouldn't you be spreading disease somewhere?

transcript.speaker: Ratbert
transcript.text: Three for three! Yes!!

setting: Dilbert's office cubicle, at his desk
situation: Ratbert stands by Dilbert's desk and boasts that his consulting job makes him richer and that he is cuter, leaving only personality to compare. Dilbert, still typing at his computer, responds by asking whether Ratbert should be off spreading disease. Ratbert cheerfully celebrates that the insult makes it three wins out of three.
punchline: Dilbert's insult about disease-spreading is taken by Ratbert as a victory, since it confirms he also beats Dilbert on personality, proving how insufferable he is.
summary: A smug rodent consultant brags about outranking his coworker in money and charm, then gleefully treats the man's barbed reply as proof he wins on every count.

file: 1998/1998-09-23_meeting objectives_sources_one objective_control fists.gif
title: Boss Can't Name Alice's Objectives

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: My sources tell me that you're not meeting your objectives.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: That's not true. Who are these sources? Name one objective I haven't met.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I don't even know what your objectives are.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Must... control... fists.

situation: The Boss accuses Alice of failing to meet her objectives, citing unnamed sources. Alice demands to know which objective she has missed, and the Boss admits he doesn't even know what her objectives are. Alice silently struggles to keep from punching him.
punchline: The Boss criticizes Alice's performance against objectives he can't even identify, leaving her barely restraining her rage.
summary: A manager faults an employee on goals he has never bothered to learn, and she fights the urge to hit him.

file: 1998/1998-06-05_budget_project_company startegy_lose hope.gif
title: Boss Withholds Budget and Strategy

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: How much budget do I have for my project?

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I can't tell you.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: If you knew what your budget was, you'd spend it all.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Can you at least tell me what our company strategy is?

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: No, I don't want you to lose hope.

setting: Office meeting table or the Boss's desk
situation: Dilbert asks his boss how much budget he has for his project, and the boss refuses to say, claiming Dilbert would spend all of it. Dilbert then asks for the company strategy, and the boss again refuses.
punchline: The boss implies the company strategy is so bad or nonexistent that revealing it would destroy employees' hope, while also treating employees as spendthrifts who can't be trusted with budget information.
summary: A manager stonewalls an employee's reasonable questions about money and direction with absurd excuses that reveal his distrust and the company's lack of any real plan.

file: 1998/1998-10-01_mordac_preventer if info services_y2k demon_not big_imagined bigger_cute_giant foot_y2k_fear_scared_culture_unknown.gif
title: Tiny Y2K Demon Turns Giant

transcript.speaker: Mordac
transcript.text: I am Mordac, the Preventer of Information Services! I summon the Y2K demon!

transcript.speaker: Demon
transcript.text: Roar roar

transcript.speaker: Mordac
transcript.text: You're not as big as I imagined. I wonder why everyone is so afraid.

transcript.speaker: Mordac
transcript.text: Cute!

situation: Mordac performs a ritual and summons the Y2K demon from his computer monitor. The demon turns out to be a tiny green creature, and Mordac wonders aloud why everyone fears it. In the last panel he holds the little demon and calls it cute, while an enormous clawed foot looms over him, revealing the demon's true size.
punchline: Mordac underestimates the Y2K threat just as it reveals its true gigantic scale, mocking people who dismissed the millennium bug as harmless.
summary: A smug IT gatekeeper conjures a pint-sized monster from his PC and dismisses the hype, unaware the real creature is towering right behind him.

file: 1998/1998-10-17_open plan office_cameras record employees_monitor phone calls_surveillance_test blood_flog them.gif
title: Catbert's Phase Two: Flogging Employees

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: We'll take away the cubicle walls and force employees to work in an "open plan" office.

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Surveillance cameras will record their every move. We'll monitor phone calls and web use. We'll even test their blood!

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Can we flog them?

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Whoa, cowboy! Wait for phase two.

situation: Catbert, the evil human resources director, presents The Boss with a plan to strip employees of privacy: open-plan offices, constant camera surveillance, monitored phone calls and web use, and even blood testing. The Boss eagerly asks if they can also flog the employees, and Catbert tells him to wait for phase two.
punchline: Even Catbert's extreme employee-control measures are only the first phase, with physical punishment held back as a later step, showing how cruel management policies can escalate.
summary: An HR cat outlines a scheme of total workplace surveillance, and his enthusiastic boss asks about whipping workers, only to be told that is saved for the sequel.

file: 1998/1998-11-14_fill out form_rules_helpless_defeated atitude_excellent job_quitting time_useless form.gif
title: Bureaucrat Counts Hours Until Quitting

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Why should I fill out this form? It would take an hour and it doesn't even apply to me.

transcript.speaker: Clerk
transcript.text: I don't make the rules. I just apply them with a helpless and defeated attitude.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: You're doing an excellent job.

transcript.speaker: Clerk
transcript.text: Seven more hours until quitting time.

setting: Office, at a clerk's desk or counter
situation: Dilbert holds a form and protests that filling it out would take an hour and doesn't even apply to him. The clerk, who is clearly demoralized, says she just enforces rules she didn't create. Dilbert sarcastically compliments her work, and she glances at her watch and counts the hours until the end of the day.
punchline: The clerk's miserable, resigned enforcement of pointless rules is the only 'excellent job' there is, and she is just waiting for the workday to end.
summary: A worn-down office clerk enforces a pointless form requirement with weary resignation while silently counting down to going home.

file: 1998/1998-09-29_employee talent show_charity_tickets_give money_forget idea.gif
title: Paying To Skip The Talent Show

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: We're having an all-employee talent show for charity. Tickets are three dollars!

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: We'll give you three dollars apiece to forget the whole thing. It works out the same.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Deal.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Ironically, math is my only talent.

situation: The Boss announces a charity talent show with three-dollar tickets. Alice counters that the employees will pay him three dollars each to cancel it, which raises the same money. The Boss accepts, and Alice remarks that math is her only talent.
punchline: Alice sidesteps the talent show by pointing out that paying to cancel it raises the same charity money, and the one skill she shows off is the math she used to get out of it.
summary: A coworker outmaneuvers a charity talent show with a quick calculation that lets everyone pay to avoid it.

file: 1998/1998-11-20_filberts mother_still loves son_loves unicrons.gif
title: Mom's Love Reduced By Unicorn Horn

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: At least I can count on my mom to love me, despite my horn.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert's Mom
transcript.text: Yes, of course, albeit not as much as before.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: How much less?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert's Mom
transcript.text: Don't worry. My love of unicorns practically covers the gap.

setting: Dilbert's mother's home, in the kitchen and living room
situation: Dilbert, who has grown a unicorn-like horn on his forehead, tells his mom he can at least count on her unconditional love. She pours coffee and admits she loves him somewhat less than before. When he asks how much less, she reassures him that her fondness for unicorns almost makes up the difference.
punchline: His mother's reassurance is backhanded: her love for him has dropped, and only her love of unicorns keeps it from dropping further, so the unconditional love he expected turns out to be conditional.
summary: A son with a horn seeks comfort from his mother and gets a backhanded answer about how much her affection has shrunk.

file: 1998/1998-04-13_two week notice_arrogant obstructionist_bore_good bye lunch_quitting_everyone happy.gif
title: Coworkers Celebrate Resignation Notice

transcript.speaker: Employee
transcript.text: I just gave my two-week notice.

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: Yes! Yes! The arrogant, obstructionist bore is history!

transcript.speaker: Employee
transcript.text: Everyone seems to be taking this rather well.

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: Count me in for the goodbye lunch!

situation: An employee tells a seated coworker that he has just handed in his two-week notice. The coworker privately cheers, pumping his fist and gleefully calling the departing employee an arrogant, obstructionist bore. Back in the last panel, the employee notes that everyone is taking the news well, and the coworker eagerly signs up for the goodbye lunch.
punchline: The resigning employee is oblivious that everyone is happy because they dislike him, and the coworker's enthusiasm for the goodbye lunch is really relief that he is leaving.
summary: A departing worker is puzzled that his colleagues seem so cheerful about his exit, not realizing they were glad to be rid of him.

file: 1998/1998-09-15_budding forearm_bone crushing handshake_hen party_insulted by wally_alice shakes hand.gif
title: Wally's Hen Party Remark Backfires

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: I've been building up my forearm so I'll have a bone-crushing handshake.

transcript.speaker: Woman with bob haircut
transcript.text: Why?

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Hey, what's this \u2014 some sort of hen party?

transcript.speaker: Woman with bob haircut
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: That was very witty, Wally. Congratulations!

situation: Alice, holding a hand exerciser, tells a female coworker she is strengthening her forearm to have a bone-crushing handshake. Wally wanders up and sarcastically asks if the two women are having some sort of hen party. Alice then congratulates him on his wit and offers a handshake, implying she is about to crush his hand.
punchline: Alice's fake praise of Wally's sexist joke sets him up for her bone-crushing handshake as payback.
summary: A sexist quip from a passing coworker earns him a mock compliment and a painful handshake from a woman who has been training for exactly this.

file: 1998/1998-01-01_nobel prize committee_theory_pig layin_nobel prize commitee_otonphay_ratbert.gif
title: Pig Latin Theory Baffles Nobel Committee

transcript.speaker: Ratbert
transcript.text: I submitted our garbage man's theory to the Nobel Prize committee.

transcript.speaker: Ratbert
transcript.text: I hope I wrote the theory right. I don't know shorthand so I used pig Latin to save time.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Nobel Prize Committee

transcript.speaker: Committee Member 1
transcript.text: What's an "otonphay"?

transcript.speaker: Committee Member 2
transcript.text: I love what you're doing with your hair.

setting: Dilbert's living room, then a Nobel Prize committee meeting room
situation: Ratbert tells Dilbert he has submitted the garbage man's theory to the Nobel Prize committee. He admits he wrote it in pig Latin because he doesn't know shorthand and wanted to save time. At the committee, one member puzzles over the strange word "otonphay" while another changes the subject to a colleague's hair.
punchline: The Nobel committee is so baffled by a scientific submission written in pig Latin that one member deflects by complimenting a colleague's wild hair, as if no one wants to admit they can't understand it.
summary: A well-meaning rodent sends a scientific theory to the Nobel judges written in a childish word game, leaving the befuddled panel more interested in each other's hairstyles.

file: 1998/1998-04-17_top priority_project classified_email_project not feasible_quality festival.gif
title: Infeasible Project Earns Quality Festival Chairmanship

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I fought to get your project classified as our top priority.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Did you get my e-mail saying the project isn't feasible?

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I'll wait until tomorrow to tell him he's chairman of the "Quality Festival."

situation: The Boss proudly tells Dilbert he fought to make Dilbert's project the company's top priority. Dilbert asks whether he received the e-mail explaining the project isn't feasible. The Boss privately decides to wait until tomorrow to punish Dilbert by naming him chairman of the dreaded Quality Festival.
punchline: The Boss responds to bad news not by reconsidering the project but by planning to punish Dilbert with a pointless, miserable committee assignment.
summary: After championing an impossible project, the boss hears it can't be done and silently plots to reward the messenger with a tedious quality-themed committee role.

file: 1998/1998-12-16_ear related cuteness_get away with crimes_pulled over_driving_cop_verbal warning_driving violations.gif
title: Dogbert Relies on Ear Cuteness

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I wonder if my ear-related cuteness will let me get away with crimes.

transcript.speaker: Police Officer
transcript.text: You passed an ambulance... on the right.

transcript.speaker: Police Officer
transcript.text: And your license is a blank piece of cardboard. I have to give you a verbal warning.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I'll cry if you do.

setting: A roadside traffic stop beside a yellow car
situation: Dogbert, driving a yellow car, muses that his cute ears might help him get away with crimes. A police officer pulls him over for passing an ambulance on the right and notes that his license is just a blank piece of cardboard. Dogbert threatens to cry if the officer gives him a warning.
punchline: Dogbert is testing whether cuteness alone can excuse serious driving violations and a fake license, and he escalates by threatening to cry to manipulate the officer.
summary: A pup in a borrowed driver's seat bets that his adorable ears can shield him from the law, even with a cardboard license.

file: 1998/1998-09-14_late to meeting_dept. meeting_change name_department name change.gif
title: Recap Trains Employee To Be Late

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I got caught in traffic.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Let me recap what you missed. We spent the past hour deciding not to change the name of our department.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: You just inadvertently trained me to be late to all meetings.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Oops.

setting: Conference room during a department meeting
situation: Wally strolls into a meeting late, claiming he was stuck in traffic. The Boss recaps what he missed: an hour spent deciding not to rename the department. Wally points out that this teaches him to skip the start of every meeting, and the Boss realizes his mistake.
punchline: The Boss's recap reveals that the missed hour accomplished nothing, which rewards Wally for being late and encourages him to keep doing it.
summary: A tardy employee learns that arriving late spares him from an hour of futile discussion, and his manager accidentally confirms it.

file: 1998/1998-11-26_job counseling_disguise fact_moron_knowledge mangement_optimization intiatives_key learnings.gif
title: Disguising Incompetence With Knowledge Management

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Job counseling

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: We'll need to disguise the fact that you're a moron.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Ironically, the best way is to become an expert in something called "knowledge management."

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: We must develop knowledge optimization initiatives to leverage our key learnings.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Smart.

setting: Dogbert's job counseling office, then a conference room
situation: Dogbert, acting as a job counselor, tells a client that his incompetence must be hidden, and recommends he become an expert in 'knowledge management.' When the client then spouts jargon in a meeting, the Pointy-Haired Boss is visibly impressed and thinks he sounds smart.
punchline: Meaningless buzzword-filled jargon is enough to make clueless managers believe someone is intelligent, so an incompetent person can hide behind it.
summary: A canine career advisor teaches a hopeless client to cover his lack of ability with trendy business-speak, and it instantly wins over a gullible manager.

file: 1998/1998-11-17_experimental medical procedures_unicron_antidepressant_therapy_instructions_will make laugh_psychology.gif
title: Unicorn Antidepressant Therapy Employee Testing

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Our new line of business is testing experimental medical procedures on employees.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Today's test is called the unicorn antidepressant therapy.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: According to the instructions, in a few minutes, I'll see something that will make me laugh.

setting: Office, in front of a large experimental medical device
situation: The Boss, wearing a strange apparatus with a horn-like device strapped to his head and a large gadget on his torso, announces that the company now tests experimental medical procedures on its own employees. He describes today's test as a unicorn antidepressant therapy. As Alice, Dilbert and Wally look on in alarm, the Boss reads the instructions and says he will soon see something that makes him laugh.
punchline: The Boss's experimental therapy is expected to make him laugh at something, and the horrified employees watching suggest that whatever he sees will be their suffering.
summary: A manager turns his staff into guinea pigs for bizarre medical experiments and cheerfully awaits the funny sight his treatment promises.

file: 1998/1998-12-22_set up date_super model_scary looking_skeleton_dogbert warns dilbert.gif
title: Supermodel Date Turns Out Skeletal

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I set up a date with the supermodel I met on the Internet.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Supermodels don't look good in person.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: That's silly.

transcript.speaker: Skeleton Date
transcript.text: I don't know how to use a vase. Do you mind if I throw those in the trash?

setting: Dilbert's living room and front doorway
situation: Dilbert tells Dogbert, who is reading on the couch, that he has a date with a supermodel he met online. Dogbert warns that supermodels look bad in person, and Dilbert dismisses this as silly. When the date arrives, she is an animated skeleton who rudely offers to throw away the flowers Dilbert brought.
punchline: Dogbert's warning proves literally true, since the supermodel is a bony skeleton, and she is also hopelessly clueless about basic etiquette like putting flowers in a vase.
summary: A man cheerfully heads into a blind date with an online model, only to be greeted at his door by a bony, tactless skeleton.

file: 1998/1998-08-01_best things in life_rat_silly_garbageman_garbage_rat jumps.gif
title: Ratbert Jumps on the Garbage

transcript.speaker: Ratbert
transcript.text: Do you mind if I jump on the garbage?

transcript.speaker: Ratbert
transcript.text: I don't know why, but when I see a fresh pile of garbage, I just want to jump up and down on it.

transcript.speaker: Garbage Man
transcript.text: The best things in life are silly.

transcript.speaker: Ratbert
transcript.text: Yee-ha!!

situation: Ratbert stands on a trash can and politely asks a garbage man if he minds him jumping on the garbage. He explains that he is inexplicably compelled to jump on fresh piles of trash. The garbage man, thinking to himself, reflects that silly things are the best, while Ratbert gleefully jumps in the can.
punchline: The garbage man's sincere musing that life's best things are silly turns a pointless act of jumping on trash into a small moment of joy.
summary: A cheerful little rat gets a garbage collector's quiet blessing to stomp around in a can of fresh trash.

file: 1998/1998-04-04_overdosing_anti depressants_induce vomiting_mission statement_ten times salary_heaving_alice punching.gif
title: Mission Statement Induces Vomiting Plan

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Alice is overdosing on antidepressants.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: We must induce vomiting.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Look at our mission statement, Alice. The people who wrote it earn ten times your salary.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: The plan worked perfectly, up to the point where all three of us were heaving and Alice was punching us.

situation: Wally and Dilbert believe Alice has overdosed on antidepressants and decide to make her vomit. Wally shows her the company mission statement and points out that its authors are paid ten times her salary. In the last panel a disheveled Dilbert reports that the plan worked until they were all retching and Alice started punching them.
punchline: Reading the corporate mission statement is so nauseating that it makes everyone vomit, and an angry Alice, reminded of the pay gap, takes it out on her coworkers.
summary: Two coworkers try to purge an apparently overdosing colleague by showing her the company's vision document, with violent and messy consequences.

file: 1998/1998-09-17_work too hard_stressed out_bored_sumerging_head in icy water_list of compalints_evil catbert.gif
title: Catbert's Unhelpful Icy Water Therapy

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: If I work too hard, I get stressed out. But if I don't work hard, I get bored.

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: I recommend submerging your head in icy water twice a day.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Wouldn't that hurt?

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Is there no end to your list of complaints?

situation: Alice, her hair as big as ever, sits with Catbert and explains that overwork stresses her out while underwork bores her. Catbert, acting as a counselor, advises her to dunk her head in icy water twice a day. When she objects that it would hurt, he snaps back that she never stops complaining.
punchline: Catbert gives absurd, painful advice and then turns the blame on the patient for complaining about it, showing he cares nothing for her wellbeing.
summary: A employee seeking advice about work stress gets a cruel suggestion from a feline counselor who then scolds her for objecting.

file: 1998/1998-06-25_dogcart the ceo_board of directors_double pay_bleat like sheep_meeting_baaa_business.gif
title: Dogbert CEO Gets Board Bleating

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Dogbert the C.E.O.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I make a motion that the board of directors double my pay.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: All in favor, bleat like sheep.

transcript.speaker: Board members
transcript.text: Ba-a-a

transcript.speaker: Board members
transcript.text: Ba-a-a

transcript.speaker: Board members
transcript.text: Ba-a-a

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I think we're missing a check or a balance somewhere.

setting: Corporate boardroom, with Wally and Dilbert listening in the hallway
situation: Dogbert, now the CEO, asks his board of directors to double his pay and tells everyone in favor to bleat like sheep. The board members all bleat in agreement. Outside the room, Wally and Dilbert overhear the baaing and Wally remarks that a check or balance seems to be missing.
punchline: The board of directors is so passive and compliant that they literally behave like sheep, rubber-stamping the CEO's self-serving pay raise with no oversight.
summary: A canine chief executive demands a raise from a flock-like board that obediently baas its approval while two employees listen from the hallway.

file: 1998/1998-09-20_personal business_lunch hour_work through lunch_take full hour_internet_business only_limited zeros and ones_technology.gif
title: Personal Internet Use Costs Zeroes
